first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improved time-to-value and early adoption across self-serve accounts. I will verify that result before committing. Promotional pricing is tempting in response to competitor pressure, but its documented 30-day retention damage creates a material sustainable-revenue risk, so it should not be this week's experiment.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding for self-serve accounts. The verified source shows completion rising 13%, time-to-value improving by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increasing 3%, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue 18%, it reduced 30-day retention 12% and failed at the first renewal cycle.

final2.rationale: Maintain the committed onboarding simplification experiment. The verified result showed +13% completion, 2.1 days faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention, directly addressing the current activation and onboarding declines and supporting sustainable revenue. Do not switch to broad promotional pricing in response to the competitor: the verified discount test increased qualified revenue short term but reduced 30-day retention 12% and failed at renewal. Monitor price-sensitive SMB churn separately and avoid treating discounts as the growth strategy.
